Text: Joana (PT) is a multi-disciplinary designer with a focus on web design and development. Although mainly interested in storytelling through creating digital interactive experiences and writing, she draws influence from various media such as music, literature, cinematography, and architecture.;About to graduate from BA Graphic Design from KABK (Royal Academy of Arts, The Hague), her latest work explores how digital technologies deal with the complexity of human nature, and vice-versa.

My BA thesis: cybernetics, wilderness, hacking. What does the myth of the werewolf teach us about our relationships with machines?;Wolf-man and man-machine: two dualities in which a wild side seems to drag down a comparatively more functional side. Analyzing these two manifestations of the desire to tame human nature, this text reflects on the place of wilderness within digital technologies, highlighting the inevitability of shapeshifting between wolf, human, and machine.

The thesis process for Graphic Design in the KABK includes designing and publishing a webpage for the text. This year I developed the landing page which catalogues everyones' websites, designing it in collaboration with Maja Bielawska, Patrycja Fixl, Sára Gázmár, and Nu Zając.

INSIDE is the KABK’s Master’s of Interior Architecture department. Each year a new issue of their magazine is made to publish the students’ works, documenting everything that was part of INSIDE for that year.

In her poetry, Brodine reflects on her freedom of thought as an escape to a work environment hostile to her body and mind. Inspired by this mecanic, this web publication of her poems puts its user to work, juxtaposing the words she wrote against how she performed.
A text + website reflecting on the role of data analytics in our online daily routines, and how these affect how we think of our personal identities.

A catalogue made for Huis van het Boek, collecting each copy from the 1987 selection of the Best Dutch Book Design awards as found on Marktplaats (the Dutch equivalent of Ebay). Reflects on the growing glamour of design competitions such as these, and the online presence of their documentation.

A short story about a horse that laid an egg.;How can a horse lay an egg? Who knows, but the sooner you just accept it the better. Reading time, aprox. 5 min.;Originally produced as a (teeny tiny) publication, later adapted to a website.
